statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-39827 (GO-2026-5016, GHSA-qpw4-5x99-6vjp): an SSH server built on golang.org/x/crypto/ssh kept channels it rejected in the connection's internal state, so an authenticated client that keeps opening channels the server rejects can grow its memory until it crashes. It is fixed in golang.org/x/crypto v0.52.0, and the Go vulnerability database names golang.org/x/crypto/ssh's channel.Reject as the vulnerable function: https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5016, https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-qpw4-5x99-6vjp, https://go.dev/issue/35127, https://go.dev/cl/781320 Read every published alertmanager-dev package for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository: 36 builds, 0.31.1-r0 to 0.35.0-r2, each for x86_64 and aarch64, each verified against the checksum in the package index. Each package installs two files, /usr/bin/alertmanager and /usr/bin/amtool, Go programs built with CGO_ENABLED=0 and -ldflags -s -w, so their functions were read from each binary's Go function table (pclntab), which lists runtime.main in every binary. Every binary was also searched as raw bytes for the package-qualified names, which also finds functions the compiler inlined. golang.org/x/crypto is v0.47.0 in 0.31.1-r0 to 0.31.1-r3, v0.49.0 in 0.31.1-r4, v0.50.0 in 0.31.1-r5 to 0.32.1-r1, v0.52.0 in 0.32.1-r2 to 0.32.2-r0, and v0.53.0 to v0.58.0 in every later build, as listed in the Go build information of both programs. The only golang.org/x/crypto packages either program links are bcrypt and blowfish (alertmanager) and bcrypt (amtool). No binary in any build has a golang.org/x/crypto/ssh function in its function table or contains the package-qualified name golang.org/x/crypto/ssh, so the vulnerable code is not present. As a positive control, the same function-table reader and byte search, run on a test program built with CGO_ENABLED=0 and -ldflags -s -w for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 against golang.org/x/crypto v0.50.0 that accepts SSH connections and rejects channels, find golang.org/x/crypto/ssh.(*channel).Reject.

statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-39827 (GO-2026-5016, GHSA-qpw4-5x99-6vjp): an authenticated SSH client that repeatedly opened channels the server rejected caused unbounded memory growth in golang.org/x/crypto/ssh, eventually crashing the server; rejected channels are now removed from the connection state. It is fixed in golang.org/x/crypto v0.52.0: https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5016, https://go.dev/issue/35127, https://go.dev/cl/781320, https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/a082jnz-LvI. Read the Go build information and the function table (with a reader of the Go symbol table that also works on stripped binaries) of every Go program in every build-dev package published in the DHI Alpine 3.23 repository: 89 builds, 2.6.4-r0 through the current 2.29.1-r1, each for x86_64 and aarch64 except 2.6.4-r0, which is published for aarch64 only, every download checked against the index checksum. Version 2.19.1-r1 is listed three times in each index; the copy the repository serves, which matches one of those entries' checksum, was read. Each package holds one file, the frontend Go program /usr/bin/build. runtime.main is found in the function table of every Go program scanned, so the tables were read. The advisory lists one vulnerable function, (*channel).Reject in golang.org/x/crypto/ssh. The frontend program contains it in every build, together with ssh.Dial and (*Client).handleChannelOpens, the client handler that rejects channel types opened by the server that it has not registered. Every build before 2.17.3-r0 links golang.org/x/crypto v0.45.0 to v0.51.0, inside the affected range; 2.17.3-r0 and every later build link v0.52.0 or newer, which carry the fix. The current 2.29.1-r1 links v0.59.0.

statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-39827 (GO-2026-5016, GHSA-qpw4-5x99-6vjp): a golang.org/x/crypto/ssh server kept every channel it rejected in the connection's channel list, so an authenticated client that repeatedly opened channels the server rejected could grow its memory without bound and crash it. It is fixed in golang.org/x/crypto v0.52.0 by commit 6c195c8 (CL 781320, the change GO-2026-5016 cites for this CVE; the commit message itself names CVE-2026-3982): https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5016, https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-qpw4-5x99-6vjp, https://go.dev/issue/35127, https://go.dev/cl/781320, https://github.com/golang/crypto/commit/6c195c8a97ae. The Go vulnerability database lists the vulnerable function as channel.Reject in the golang.org/x/crypto/ssh package. We read every published external-dns-dev package for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository: 33 builds, 0.20.0-r0 to the current 0.24.0-r5, each for x86_64 and aarch64 and each matching its repository index checksum. Each package holds one file, /usr/bin/external-dns (a full listing, symlinks included), a statically linked Go program (no program interpreter and no shared-library dependencies) built with CGO_ENABLED=0. Its Go build information lists golang.org/x/crypto v0.45.0 in 0.20.0-r0 to 0.20.0-r3, v0.49.0 in 0.20.0-r4 to 0.21.0-r1, v0.50.0 in 0.21.0-r2 and 0.21.0-r3, v0.51.0 in 0.21.0-r4, and v0.52.0 or later from 0.21.0-r5 on (v0.58.0 in the current build), with no replace directive for it, so the builds before 0.21.0-r5 are in the advisory's version range. The program does not contain the vulnerable code. A Go function-table (pclntab) reader finds runtime.main in every build, which shows the listing works on that file, but no function of the golang.org/x/crypto/ssh package and none of golang.org/x/crypto/ssh/agent in any build: the only name under golang.org/x/crypto/ssh is golang.org/x/crypto/ssh/terminal.init, the initializer of the separate ssh/terminal package, in 0.20.0-r0 to 0.21.0-r13. A byte search of every build, which also catches the names of inlined functions, finds no "golang.org/x/crypto/ssh." at all. As a positive control, the same reader and byte search find ssh.(*channel).Reject in a test program we built against golang.org/x/crypto v0.51.0, the last release before the fix, for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64. The golang.org/x/crypto version in the build information therefore does not make this package affected.

CVE-2026-39827 (GO-2026-5016): An authenticated SSH client that repeatedly opened channels which were rejected by the server caused unbounded memory growth, eventually crashing the server process and affecting all connected users. Rejected channels are now properly removed from the connection's internal state and released for garbage collection. The flaw is in the golang.org/x/crypto/ssh package and is fixed in golang.org/x/crypto v0.52.0 (https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5016, https://go.dev/issue/35127, https://go.dev/cl/781320, https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/a082jnz-LvI). This package is the Go 1.26 toolchain. The Go source tree it ships vendors a few golang.org/x/crypto packages for the standard library under /usr/lib/go/src/vendor, and its cmd tree vendors no golang.org/x/crypto package. In no published build is golang.org/x/crypto/ssh among them. Checked every published golang-1.26-dev package for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository (1.26.1-r2 to 1.26.11-r1, x86_64 and aarch64), together with the doc and oci-config subpackages built from the same source: none contains a golang.org/x/crypto/ssh directory or source file, and no ELF file in them (including the go and gofmt commands and the tools under /usr/lib/go/pkg/tool) contains golang.org/x/crypto/ssh code or symbols. A Go program that uses golang.org/x/crypto/ssh takes it from its own golang.org/x/crypto requirement, not from the toolchain, so it is fixed by upgrading golang.org/x/crypto in that program.
